text.en:
Grandmother poured rice into a big plate. "There are tiny stones in it," she said.
She picked out the stones, then washed the rice. The water turned cloudy, and she poured it out slowly while the rice stayed in the vessel.
"Every mixture needs the right method," she told Varun.

A mixture has two or more things together. We separate them when one part is not wanted or when each part is useful.
Hand-picking removes stones from rice or dal. Winnowing uses wind to separate light husk from heavy grain. Sieving separates small particles from bigger ones, such as flour from husk.
Sedimentation and decantation: when a muddy water is left, heavy mud settles at the bottom (sedimentation) and the clear water is poured off (decantation). Filtration uses filter paper or a cloth to separate solid bits from a liquid.
Evaporation separates a dissolved solid from a liquid. When salty water is heated, the water becomes vapour and salt is left behind. This is how salt is made from sea water.
Many mixtures need more than one method. We choose the method by what is different about the parts: size, weight, or whether they dissolve.
A mixture has two or more things. We separate them using a difference between them.
Wind separates light husk from heavy grain. This is winnowing. A sieve separates small particles from big ones.
Let muddy water stand. Mud settles, and we pour off the clear water. A cloth or filter paper can also remove bits.
Heat salty water. The water turns into vapour and salt is left. This is evaporation.

problem.en: A bowl has salt dissolved in water. How can we get the salt back?

text.en: Salt is dissolved, so filtration will not work.

why.en: The salt passes through the filter with the water.

text.en: Heat the water slowly so it evaporates.
The salt is left behind in the bowl.

prompt.en: A friend says we can separate salt from salty water with filter paper. Is he right?

requiredIdeas.en: No, because salt is dissolved and passes through the filter paper.
We should evaporate the water to get the salt.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking filtration separates anything from a liquid.

points.en: Mixtures are separated using a difference between the parts.
Winnowing, sieving, filtration, sedimentation and decantation separate solids.
Evaporation separates a dissolved solid from a liquid.
